title: Canary Glance: Cohort Telemetry Hub for Rollouts
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a Console-first telemetry hub (Canary Glance) that surfaces per-route and per-cohort signal for model rollouts: canary/A-B cohorts, shadow traffic, and automatic rollback triggers. The hub provides heatmaps, cohort delta visualizations, trace linking to distributed traces, and a decision panel to approve/abort/auto-rollback. Goal: reduce time-to-detect and mean-time-to-recover for bad model variants while giving PMs/engineers a single pane for rollout decisions.
background: Current rollout visibility is fragmented: token-level cost and latency charts exist, but there is no unified cohort diff visualization or fast drill-down from cohort delta to example traces. Customers running canaries and shadow traffic have asked for: 1) fast per-route cohort comparisons, 2) significance-aware drift highlighting, 3) trace linking from cohort samples to the infra trace, and 4) an operator-friendly rollback flow tied to policies. This ticket scopes the product and acceptance criteria and coordinates Eng/Design work.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows a default 'Canary Glance' view for any active rollout with: throughput, p50/p95 latency, error rate, and token cost broken out by cohort (control vs candidate)

Cohort delta visualization (heatmap + ranked metrics) highlights metrics that exceed configured thresholds and computes statistical significance (chi-sq or bootstrap) before surfacing as actionable signals
Users can click any cohort cell to open a trace-linked sample panel that shows n=20 request examples, model outputs, prompt/metadata, and a link to the distributed trace in Tempo/Jaeger
Rollout decision panel supports: manual approve/abort, schedule rollback, and auto-rollback policies that trigger on combined SLO breach + metric delta for X minutes
Shadow traffic summary shows shadow-only anomalies and annotates which cohort changes were only observed in shadowed requests
All telemetry respects tenancy and does not expose customer prompt text by default; sample capture is redaction-aware and only enabled when allowed by policy
Telemetry queries must complete within 3s for 30m window and 6s for 24h window in Console under normal load
Documentation (Console help + runbook) and an internal postmortem playbook are linked from the UI
implementation_notes: Backend: new telemetry aggregation endpoints (rollout/metrics/v1) that fetch per-route per-cohort aggregates from the metrics pipeline. Add lightweight significance computation in the metrics service to avoid heavy client work. UI: new Canary Glance page under Deployments with heatmap, cohort timeline, example list, and decision panel. Instrumentation: add cohort tag to request logs and ensure KV cache metrics are reported by cohort. Work with infra to add a 30s pre-aggregated cache for the 1h window to meet UI latency targets.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (MVP): read-only Canary Glance with aggregated metrics, heatmap, and sample popover. Phase 2: trace linking, shadow summary, and decision panel with manual controls. Phase 3: auto-rollback policies and runbook automation. Rollout to internal teams first, then gradual enablement for customers via feature flag. Monitor: launch with an alert on Console API error rate and query tail latency.
metrics_to_track: error rate by cohort (5xx + model errors)
token cost per request by cohort
top-k output divergence score by cohort (BLEU/embedding-diff or chosen metric)
trace span duration and percentiles linked to sampled requests

Eng Metrics: add cohort tags to metrics pipeline and expose new aggregation API endpoints
Eng UI: implement Canary Glance page, heatmap, and sample panel
Eng Runtime: ensure request path adds rollout cohort metadata and safe-sample hook
SRE: provision pre-aggregation cache and add observability for query latency
Security: review sample capture redaction and data retention policy
Docs: write Console help and internal postmortem playbook
open_risks: Sampling bias: heatmap signals depend on representative sampling; low-volume cohorts may produce noisy deltas
Privacy: captured examples may contain PII or sensitive prompts — must gate and redact by default
Query latency: naive joins across long time windows could blow up Console latency without pre-aggregation
Auto-rollback sensitivity: poorly-tuned thresholds risk flapping (rollback/restore loops) — require cooldowns and hysteresis
